home.title: DataCite JSON and JSON-LD
home.tagline: Research metadata in JSON and JSON-LD.
home.lead: Explore the GFZ / ERNIE profiles for DataCite 4.7. Choose JSON to work with metadata attributes, or JSON-LD to work with Linked Data.
home.heading: Choose the format you work with
home.description: Both views explain the same DataCite concepts. Their field paths, examples, and validation instructions follow the selected format.

cards.title: JSON
cards.description: Read the DataCite attributes, their required fields, allowed values, and JSON Schema rules.

cards.title: JSON-LD
cards.description: Understand the compact attrs/value profile, its context, field mappings, and Linked Data meaning.

differences.title: JSON Schema checks the attributes
differences.description: The published schema checks structure, field types, required fields, allowed values, and conditional rules. Enable URI format checks in your validator.

differences.title: A context gives Linked Data meaning
differences.description: The JSON-LD context maps terms to IRIs and defines collections and value types. Processing the context does not check DataCite required fields or cardinalities.

differences.title: These are GFZ / ERNIE profiles
differences.description: The guides describe the published local JSON schema and compact JSON-LD profile. The official DataCite documentation defines the metadata standard. The separate Schema.org JSON-LD embedded in landing pages serves discovery.

json.title: Start with a clear metadata record.
json.description: This guide describes the GFZ / ERNIE DataCite 4.7 JSON attributes profile for metadata curators and developers. The field rules are read from the exact published JSON schema.

steps.title: Start small
steps.description: Open the minimal draft. Add your own metadata and a DOI when one is assigned.

steps.title: Find the right field
steps.description: Browse a topic or search for a field. Each entry shows its JSON path, child fields, and actual schema rules.

steps.title: Check the record
steps.description: Validate the attributes object with a Draft 2020-12 validator. Registration also applies DataCite API checks.

rules.title: Validate the attributes
rules.description: The JSON schema describes the attributes object. A DataCite JSON API document wraps that object inside data.attributes.

rules.title: Keep the precision you know
rules.description: Use four-digit publication years as strings. Dates may include a year, month, day, date-time, or an open or closed range. Do not invent missing precision.

rules.title: Use the whole record
rules.description: Some rules depend on another field. A related metadata scheme may be stated only for HasMetadata or IsMetadataFor relations. Validate the complete record to check these conditions.

rules.title: Metadata fields only
rules.description: This profile allows the listed metadata properties. Raw DataCite API responses may also contain administrative fields such as state, prefix, or url. Keep those separate before validating the metadata.

jsonld.title: Connect the metadata to Linked Data.
jsonld.description: This guide describes the compact GFZ / ERNIE attrs/value profile. Browse DataCite concepts, see their actual JSON-LD paths, and follow each term to its meaning. Required labels and value rules refer to the DataCite attributes after conversion.

steps.title: Use the matching context
steps.description: The example points to a fixed published context. Keep the document structure and the context together.

steps.title: Read the wrappers
steps.description: Collections have plural and singular keys. A scalar uses value; its metadata uses attrs. The examples show the exact structure.

steps.title: Process and validate
steps.description: Process the document with a JSON-LD 1.1 processor. To check DataCite fields, also validate the supported profile and the converted JSON attributes.

rules.title: One item or several
rules.description: A singular collection key holds an object for one item, or an array for several. [] in this guide covers both compact forms. Polygon vertices always use an array.

rules.title: Order and meaning
rules.description: Creators and polygon vertices use ordered lists. Other collections use their context-defined meaning. Property IRIs and value types come from the published context.

rules.title: Fields follow DataCite concepts
rules.description: The tree groups related metadata concepts. JSON-LD paths show the actual locations, including attrs and value. Rule labels describe the converted attributes, rather than a separate JSON-LD validation schema.

rules.title: Check all layers
rules.description: JSON-LD expansion gives the data meaning. A supported-profile check and JSON Schema validation of the converted attributes check different requirements.

rules.objectAlternative: This field has more than one supported form. Its child fields apply to the object form.
rules.dependentRequired: When {field} is present, {dependencies} must also be present.
rules.fieldDescription: The {field} value in this DataCite metadata record.

notes.title: A published local profile
notes.description: This reference uses the checksummed schema and context served by GFZ Data Services. It describes their actual rules and the supported compact profile.

notes.title: Drafts and registration
notes.description: The JSON schema permits a draft without doi. Registering a DOI requires a DOI and further DataCite API checks. These examples do not perform a registration.

notes.title: Context provenance
notes.description: The JSON-LD context is derived from TIB DataCite Linked Data, maintained and created by @selgebali, under CC BY 4.0. The manifest records the source commit, checksums, and profile adjustments.

jsonldNotes.title: JSON-only fields
jsonldNotes.description: The compact exporter derives identifier and @id from doi. It does not export the separate JSON identifiers or container fields, or language properties on creator and contributor objects.

jsonldNotes.title: Use the supported profile
jsonldNotes.description: The context also contains compatibility terms. The field list follows the actual exporter and supported importer profile; the presence of a term in a context does not make every use of it supported.

jsonldNotes.title: Names and URI spellings
jsonldNotes.description: Paths show the spelling emitted by the exporter, including attrs and value. The supported importer also recognises documented historical URI aliases.

json.title: Validate a JSON record
json.description: Use a JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 validator. For the Python example, install jsonschema with its format dependencies: pip install "jsonschema[format]".

steps.title: Select the attributes
steps.description: Use the standalone attributes object. For a JSON API export, select data.attributes first.

steps.title: Choose the matching schema
steps.description: Use the fixed schema URL for repeatable validation, or download that schema for offline use.

steps.title: Enable format checks
steps.description: URI format checks need a format checker in addition to the schema rules.

steps.title: Apply registration checks
steps.description: A schema-valid draft is a starting point. DOI registration also needs a DOI and the DataCite API requirements.

json.code:
import json
from urllib.request import urlopen
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator, FormatChecker

with urlopen("{schemaUrl}") as response:
    schema = json.load(response)
with open("metadata.json", encoding="utf-8") as source:
    record = json.load(source)
attributes = record["data"]["attributes"] if "data" in record else record
Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)
Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=FormatChecker()).validate(attributes)
print("Valid DataCite attributes")

jsonld.title: Process and validate a JSON-LD record
jsonld.description: JSON-LD meaning and DataCite field validation are separate checks. Use a JSON-LD 1.1 processor with the matching context, and a converter that supports this exact compact profile.

steps.title: Read valid JSON
steps.description: Parse the document and keep its @context, @type, and any DOI-based @id.

steps.title: Check the supported profile
steps.description: Check the attrs/value structure, allowed fields, collection forms, and agreement between identifier and @id.

steps.title: Process the context
steps.description: Expand the document with a JSON-LD 1.1 processor. Check the resulting IRIs, value types, and lists. Expansion alone does not check DataCite required fields.

steps.title: Validate the attributes
steps.description: Use the ERNIE importer or a compatible converter to recover DataCite attributes. Normalise coordinates and year representations, then validate with the JSON schema. Registration applies further checks.

doi.label: DOI

types.label: Resource type

resourceType.label: Specific resource type
resourceType.description: A more specific description, such as geophysical observations or a laboratory protocol.

identifiers.label: Identifiers
identifiers.description: Identifiers stated explicitly in this attributes record. Each identifier includes its type.

familyName.label: Family name

affiliation.label: Affiliations

affiliationIdentifierScheme.label: Affiliation identifier scheme

titles.label: Titles

titleType.label: Title type

lang.label: Language tag
lang.description: The language of this text, expressed as a language tag such as en.

publisher.label: Publisher
publisher.description: The organisation that publishes, holds, or makes the resource available.

publisherIdentifier.label: Publisher identifier

publisherIdentifierScheme.label: Publisher identifier scheme
publisherIdentifierScheme.description: The identifier system used for the publisher.

publicationYear.label: Publication year
publicationYear.description: The year when this resource became, or will become, publicly available. Use a four-digit string.

subjects.label: Subjects
subjects.description: Keywords, classifications, or topics that describe the resource.

subject.label: Subject
subject.description: A keyword or classification term for the resource.

subjectScheme.label: Subject scheme
subjectScheme.description: The name of the vocabulary or classification used for the subject.

valueUri.label: Value URI
valueUri.description: A URI identifying this specific term within a vocabulary.

classificationCode.label: Classification code

contributorType.label: Contributor role
contributorType.description: The role of this contributor in relation to the resource.

dates.label: Dates
dates.description: Dates relevant to the resource or its metadata. The date type explains each date.

date.label: Date
date.description: A date, date-time, or date range. Keep the precision that is known.

dateType.label: Date type
dateType.description: The event or activity described by this date.

dateInformation.label: Date information
dateInformation.description: A short explanation of the date, when further context is helpful.

language.label: Resource language

alternateIdentifiers.label: Alternate identifiers
alternateIdentifiers.description: Other identifiers that refer to the same resource.

alternateIdentifier.label: Alternate identifier

alternateIdentifierType.label: Alternate identifier type
alternateIdentifierType.description: The system or kind of the alternate identifier.

relatedIdentifiers.label: Related identifiers
relatedIdentifiers.description: Identifiers for other resources related to this one.

relatedIdentifier.label: Related identifier
relatedIdentifier.description: The identifier of another related resource.

relatedIdentifierType.label: Related identifier type

relationTypeInformation.label: Relation explanation

relatedMetadataScheme.label: Related metadata scheme

schemeType.label: Scheme type
schemeType.description: The kind of schema used by the related metadata record.

sizes.label: Sizes

formats.label: Formats
formats.description: The file formats or physical forms in which the resource is available.

version.label: Version

rightsList.label: Rights and licences

rightsUri.label: Rights URI

geoLocations.description: Places or geographic areas relevant to the resource.

geoLocationPlace.label: Place name
geoLocationPlace.description: A place name or a short description of the location.

pointLatitude.label: Latitude

eastBoundLongitude.label: Eastern longitude
eastBoundLongitude.description: The longitude of the eastern boundary in decimal degrees.

southBoundLatitude.label: Southern latitude
southBoundLatitude.description: The latitude of the southern boundary in decimal degrees.

northBoundLatitude.label: Northern latitude
northBoundLatitude.description: The latitude of the northern boundary in decimal degrees.

fundingReferences.description: Funding organisations and awards that supported the resource.

funderName.label: Funder name
funderName.description: The name of the organisation that provided funding.

funderIdentifier.label: Funder identifier
funderIdentifier.description: A persistent identifier for the funding organisation.

funderIdentifierType.label: Funder identifier type
funderIdentifierType.description: The identifier system used for the funder.

awardNumber.label: Award number
awardNumber.description: The grant or award number assigned by the funder.

awardUri.label: Award URI
awardUri.description: A web address for the grant or award.

awardTitle.label: Award title
awardTitle.description: The name of the funded project or award.

relatedItems.label: Related items
relatedItems.description: Detailed metadata about related publications or other resources.

relatedItemType.label: Related item type
relatedItemType.description: The broad resource type of the related item.

relatedItemIdentifier.label: Related item identifier
relatedItemIdentifier.description: The identifier of the related item, with information about its identifier system.

relatedItemIdentifierType.label: Related item identifier type
relatedItemIdentifierType.description: The identifier system used by the related item.

volume.label: Volume
volume.description: The volume in which the related item appears.

issue.label: Issue
issue.description: The issue in which the related item appears.

number.label: Number
number.description: A number used to identify the related item within its publication.

numberType.label: Number type
numberType.description: The kind of number used for the related item.

firstPage.label: First page
firstPage.description: The first page of the related item.

lastPage.label: Last page
lastPage.description: The last page of the related item.

edition.label: Edition
edition.description: The edition of the related item.

container.label: Container

type.label: Container type
type.description: The kind of container that holds this resource.

$.label: DataCite attributes
$.description: The metadata attributes for one resource. For a DataCite JSON API document, use the object inside data.attributes.
notes: Only the listed metadata properties are allowed. For an API response, select data.attributes and separate fields used only for API administration.

$.publisher.label: Publisher
$.publisher.description: The organisation that publishes, holds, or makes the resource available.
notes: The JSON profile also accepts a plain publisher name as a string. Use the object form shown here when you need an identifier or want to convert the record to this JSON-LD profile.

$.identifiers.label: Identifiers
$.identifiers.description: Identifiers stated explicitly in this attributes record. Each identifier includes its type.
notes: The compact JSON-LD export creates its identifier from doi. It does not export this separate identifiers collection.

$.container.label: Container
$.container.description: Information about the publication or container that holds this resource.
notes: This JSON property is outside the compact JSON-LD export profile.

$.relatedIdentifiers.label: Related identifiers
$.relatedIdentifiers.description: Identifiers for other resources related to this one.
notes: A metadata scheme may be stated only for HasMetadata or IsMetadataFor. URL and URN identifier types require a URI value. These conditions are checked on the complete record.
Use relationTypeInformation to explain Other relations. The published JSON schema does not make it required when Other is selected.

$.relatedIdentifiers[].relationTypeInfor.label: Relation explanation
$.relatedIdentifiers[].relationTypeInfor.description: A short explanation of a relation described as Other.
notes: Use this property to explain Other relations. The published JSON schema keeps it optional and does not impose a relationType condition on this property.

$.relatedItems.label: Related items
$.relatedItems.description: Detailed metadata about related publications or other resources.
notes: A metadata scheme may be stated only for HasMetadata or IsMetadataFor. URL and URN identifier types require a URI value. These conditions are checked on the complete record.
Use relationTypeInformation to explain Other relations. The published JSON schema does not make it required when Other is selected.

$.relatedItems[].relationTypeInformation.label: Relation explanation
$.relatedItems[].relationTypeInformation.description: A short explanation of a relation described as Other.
notes: Use this property to explain Other relations. The published JSON schema keeps it optional and does not impose a relationType condition on this property.

$.creators[].lang.label: Language tag
$.creators[].lang.description: The language of this text, expressed as a language tag such as en.
notes: This property is accepted by the JSON schema but is not carried into the compact JSON-LD profile.

$.contributors[].lang.label: Language tag
$.contributors[].lang.description: The language of this text, expressed as a language tag such as en.
notes: This property is accepted by the JSON schema but is not carried into the compact JSON-LD profile.

$.relatedItems[].creators[].lang.label: Language tag
$.relatedItems[].creators[].lang.description: The language of this text, expressed as a language tag such as en.
notes: This property is accepted by the JSON schema but is not carried into the compact JSON-LD profile.

$.relatedItems[].contributors[].lang.label: Language tag
$.relatedItems[].contributors[].lang.description: The language of this text, expressed as a language tag such as en.
notes: This property is accepted by the JSON schema but is not carried into the compact JSON-LD profile.

$.relatedItems[].relatedItemIdentifier.r.label: Related item identifier
$.relatedItems[].relatedItemIdentifier.r.description: The identifier of the related item, with information about its identifier system.
notes: Use a URI value when relatedItemIdentifierType is URL or URN. Other identifier types follow their own identifier conventions.

$.relatedIdentifiers[].relatedIdentifier.label: Related identifier
$.relatedIdentifiers[].relatedIdentifier.description: The identifier of another related resource.
notes: Use a URI value when relatedIdentifierType is URL or URN. Other identifier types follow their own identifier conventions.

jsonldInterface.itemsAnyOf: After conversion to DataCite JSON, each array item must match at least one of these alternatives.

jsonldInterface.title: DataCite JSON-LD
jsonldInterface.fragmentNote: Fragment from the extended record. The full record declares @context and @type.
jsonldInterface.requiredExplanation: Required labels describe the converted DataCite attributes. The context maps terms and does not enforce required fields. The format notes explain the wrappers.

jsonldRoot.label: DataCite JSON-LD record
jsonldRoot.description: One resource in the compact GFZ / ERNIE JSON-LD profile, with its context and Linked Data meaning.

jsonldPublisherNotes: Use value for the publisher name and attrs for its identifier, scheme, and language. This compact profile uses a publisher object.
keywordNote: This entry describes the supported compact profile. The JSON-LD context is not a validation schema.

context.label: JSON-LD context
context.description: The fixed published context that gives meaning to the terms in this profile.

type.name: @type
type.label: Resource class
type.description: The resource class. This profile emits Resource, which the context maps to the TIB DataCite Resource class.

id.name: @id
id.label: Resource IRI
id.description: The DOI resolver URL for this resource. When present, it must agree with identifier.value.
